solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One panics about the wings touching fog

blocks.note: alar is the adjective meaning relating to wings
mist is a thin fog

explanation.surface: Someone flaps anxiously about the wings of a plane as it flies into fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About the wings' looks like a location, but it is a definition of the rare adjective ALAR; 'touching' just puts the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist is a person who spreads or gives way to needless fear, someone quick to panic.

clue.text: Maybe Moroccan landscape extremely suitable for growing crops

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: a Moroccan may be an Arab, a definition by example
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Moroccan landscape is described as ideal farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' warns that Moroccan is only one example of an Arab, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is ploughable soil used for cultivating cereal and other field harvests.

clue.text: Worship without a prayer? The preacher ultimately is a cheat

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so a letter is taken away
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: to adulate is to worship or flatter excessively
taken as written, then removed
last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A preacher who worships without praying turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a prayer' reads as an idiom for hopelessness, but it splits across two jobs: 'without a' removes a letter, and 'prayer' is one of three words whose endings are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer cheats on a spouse, so in everyday speech such a person is called a cheat.

clue.text: Bug nestling in humid genitalia

indicators.note: something nestling in something else sits snugly within it, so the letters are tucked inside the following words

blocks.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An insect has settled somewhere warm, damp and embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'humid' and the start of 'genitalia'.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny biting fly, and bug is a general informal word for any small insect.

clue.text: Fool on the phone getting help

indicators.note: on the phone we only hear words, so the answer is chosen by its sound, not spelling

blocks.note: a sucker is a gullible person, a fool

explanation.surface: A gullible person rings up a helpline to get assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech SUCKER and SUCCOUR sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is a formal word for assistance or relief given in time of need.

clue.text: Recommendation to see trailer: it’s gripping

blocks.note: a film trailer is an advertisement, AD for short
a vice is a workshop tool that grips things

explanation.surface: Someone recommends watching a film trailer because it is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's gripping' reads as praise for the trailer, but it is a cryptic description of the clamping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance offered to someone about what they should do, a synonym for recommendation.

clue.text: Act to save vital organ and it’s saved

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a deed is an act
the liver is a vital organ

explanation.surface: A surgeon acts to save a patient's vital organ, and the patient survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To save' reads as rescuing the organ, but it means holding it; the act splits in half around the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delivered is to be rescued or set free, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Interested in acquiring Ravel’s first prelude

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only
to acquire something is to take it in, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: to be into something is to be interested in it
opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A music lover takes an interest in the opening prelude by the composer Ravel.
explanation.walkthrough: INTO is informal for interested in; R goes inside it before the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is short for introduction, the opening passage of a piece of music, just like a prelude.

clue.text: Previously working as a model? That’s revealing

blocks.note: ex means former or previously
a model poses for artists or photographers

explanation.surface: Someone's past as a model comes out, and it's quite a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' works both as the definition and as a wink at modelling in little clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing and revealing both mean uncovering something so that it can be seen.

clue.text: Quad redesigned with cute water channel

indicators.note: something redesigned has been laid out afresh, so its letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college quadrangle is remodelled with a pretty little water feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two lots of fodder; both words are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a bridge or conduit built to carry water across country, a man-made water channel.

clue.text: Dump is full, needs emptying. Shame having to go back

indicators.note: emptying a word removes everything inside it, leaving just its outer shell
going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
'it's a shame' and 'it's a pity' mean the same

explanation.surface: The local tip is full and must be cleared; a pity that everyone has to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump is full' reads like a rubbish-tip notice, but Dump is a verb. Fly-tipping is the British term for illegally dumping rubbish in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly-tip is to dispose of waste illegally on public or private land, a specific kind of dumping.

clue.text: Key turned up inside duffel coat

indicators.note: inside means contained within, so the letters lie within the following words
in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A lost key turns up in the pocket of a duffel coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' sounds like finding the key, but in this down clue it means read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the musical symbol fixing pitch on a stave, and key is a looser musical sense for it.

clue.text: Machine producing fifty articles

blocks.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A factory machine turns out fifty items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests manufactured goods; here it means the grammatical words A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a workshop device that rotates material so it can be cut and shaped.

clue.text: Not aware plain cover for Elvis is oddly missing

indicators.note: a cover goes around what it protects, so one piece wraps another
with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the even-positioned ones remain

blocks.note: plain means clear or obvious
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone fails to notice that the plain sleeve for an Elvis record has strangely vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a record sleeve or a cover version; here plain wraps round what survives of the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means being unconscious of what is happening around one, lacking awareness.

clue.text: Suitable for each

blocks.note: pro is Latin for in favour of
per as in 'a pound per person'

explanation.walkthrough: Three small words read like a fragment of a sentence; each one does a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means appropriate or correct for the circumstances, a close synonym of fitting.

clue.text: Detectives told to transfer ownership

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the answer matches the words by their sound

blocks.note: private eyes are private detectives

explanation.surface: Police detectives are ordered to hand over some property.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'private eyes' quickly and it runs together into the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To privatise is to move a business or service from state control into private hands, a specific transfer.

clue.text: Return of monarchy from abroad

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
a monarch's reign is their rule

explanation.surface: An exiled royal family comes back from overseas to rule again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' looks like the whole restoration theme, but 'Return' acts only on the small word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign describes something originating in or coming from another country.

clue.text: Perception of home schooling

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
tuition is teaching

explanation.surface: People have views about home schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home schooling' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is an instinctive understanding or insight gained without conscious reasoning, a kind of perception.

clue.text: Dad’s back with mum? It’s looking likely

indicators.note: going back means going the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: Pa is an informal name for a father
a mum is one parent

explanation.surface: A father has come home to his wife, and a reconciliation seems on the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's back' sounds like a return home; the 's is 'is'. Mum is a parent by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means seeming to be real or true on the evidence, which is looking probable.

clue.text: Standard accessories for events

blocks.note: par is the normal or expected standard, as in golf
neckties are clothing accessories

explanation.surface: Routine add-ons are recommended for special occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are ordinary synonyms; 'accessories' covers ties as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties are social gatherings or celebrations, which count as events on a calendar.

clue.text: Herb sausage America dismissed

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation for the country

explanation.surface: A herb-flavoured sausage was turned down by the American market.
explanation.walkthrough: Take USA out of SAUSAGE and what remains is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is an aromatic grey-green plant used in cooking, commonly in stuffing and sausages.

clue.text: Bedsit renovated with bathroom fixtures

indicators.note: renovating a room rearranges and rebuilds it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small rented room has been done up with new bathroom fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat combining bedroom and sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidets are low washbasins installed in bathrooms, so they are plumbing fittings of that room.

clue.text: Times coverage of isolated rubbish

indicators.note: coverage wraps around its subject, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: times as in multiplication, three by four
isolated means on one's own

explanation.surface: A newspaper, The Times, reports on remote communities and is accused of writing nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign read aloud as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is informal American slang for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: About food served up, it’s fast food

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: re means regarding or about
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Something about food being served, and it turns out to be takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' is kitchen language, but in a down clue it turns the pieces upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A burger is a minced-beef patty in a bun, the classic quick takeaway dish.

clue.text: Both sides keeping little money to pursue a special messenger

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another
to pursue is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
R and L for right and left
change is small coins

explanation.surface: A courier works for both parties in a deal, pocketing a small fee.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANGE sits between R and L, and the whole follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel comes from the Greek for messenger, and an archangel is one of highest rank, like Gabriel.

clue.text: Sea travel reportedly needs them

indicators.note: a report is heard rather than seen, so the answer is matched by its sound

blocks.note: a cruise is a holiday voyage by sea

explanation.surface: Sea voyages cannot run without certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back to what sea travel needs: ship's sailors, which is also the word being sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Crews are the teams of sailors who work a ship, which any voyage requires, so 'them' refers to these.

clue.text: Occasionally taking paid time out to say goodbye

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone taking paid leave now and then waves farewell to colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid time out' sounds like holiday leave; its even letters spell the French farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell used in English, meaning farewell or until God.

clue.text: Everyone is getting round to this island

indicators.note: getting round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: all means everyone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everybody eventually visits this particular island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting round to' reads as an idiom for finally doing something; the 'to' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or chain of islets enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Refer to Goliath’s comeback as sickening

indicators.note: a comeback is a coming back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to cite a source is to refer to it
Goliath is this puzzle's setter, so the setter is me

explanation.surface: Someone describes the giant Goliath's return as nauseating.
explanation.walkthrough: Goliath is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for ME rather than the Biblical giant.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic causes vomiting, so it is sickening in the literal sense of making one ill.

clue.text: Giving gifts, finish in debt

blocks.note: to finish is to end
to be owing is to be in debt

explanation.surface: A generous giver ends up owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are straight synonyms placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowing means bestowing money or property, typically a lasting donation to an institution.

clue.text: Opportunity to sample special treats

indicators.note: something special has been specially prepared, so its letters are made up afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chance to try some special delicacies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' looks like it describes the treats, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small introductory experience or portion that lets someone try something out.

clue.text: Look at ship’s make-up

blocks.note: to eye something is to look at it
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone invites us to inspect how a ship is constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' reads as structure or composition, but it means cosmetics; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is a cosmetic drawn along the lashes, one of many cosmetics.
